title: powerops deploy apply --format json
description: The JSON written by 'powerops deploy apply --format json': what a dry run would import, or what an apply imported, the state of each planned cloud flow afterwards, and the Copilot Studio agents of the imported zips. It never holds an environment id or URL, a folder path, a connection id, an environment variable value, the --target value or pac's output text; only the target's friendly name, the tool version, file names, solution names, flow names, agent names, states and the reviewed plan's hash. Keep the report in private places, because the names can still identify a tenant.

tool.description: The version 'powerops --version' prints. Plan and apply must run the same version.

applied.description: True whenever --apply was given, including refusals and failures; 'status' says what happened. False for a dry run.

target.description: The target environment's friendly name. Never its id or URL. Empty when the plan file was made by another powerops version, because none of its fields is trusted then.

hash.description: The reviewed plan file's hash, never the new plan's. Empty when the plan file was made by another powerops version.

status.description: refused: nothing was imported (exit 1), because the plan file is blocked or from another version, the new plan's hash differs, the new plan is blocked, or, with --require-reviews, a zip the plan imports is not covered by both review reports of one plan folder or no readable docs/plans exists. planned: a dry run (exit 0). imported: the imports ran, or, with the message 'Nothing was imported: every solution was skipped.', none was needed and nothing changed; see message and flows for exit 1 and 3. failed: an import failed, pac was not found, or a file changed before its import, or an import timed out, which leaves its row unknown (exit 3); there is no rollback.

message.description: Why a run stopped, or null. For a failure it says there is no rollback and names the imported solutions; after good imports, a second read that failed starts with 'The imports succeeded.'. With status imported, 'Nothing was imported: every solution was skipped.' means every solution was a skip and nothing changed.

appliedAt.description: The UTC time, to the second, at which an --apply run passed its checks and started importing, from the clock of the machine that ran it. Set when status is imported or failed; null for planned and refused, which imported nothing.

executor.description: The route the run took, as the caller reports it: action with --github-run (the GitHub Action), mcp when the MCP tool deploy_apply ran it, else cli. Provenance, not authentication: nothing checks it, and a person at a shell can pass --github-run.

approval.description: How the yes to the import was given, as the caller reports it; null without --apply. Provenance, not authentication: it holds no identity, and nothing in it proves who approved.

mode.description: form: the MCP tool passed the plan hash that the user's form showed (the user typed the environment's name). action: --github-run was given. cli: neither, so the person who ran the command is the only approval, and nothing checks it.

receipt.description: Opaque text. For the Action it is the repository, run, attempt and job environment, which point at GitHub's own record of who approved the run; for cli and form it is null.

solutions.description: In plan order; empty when the run was refused before the re-plan.

order.description: The position in the import order, from 1.

zip.description: The zip's file name, without a folder.

action.description: The new plan's action; a skip imports nothing.

import.description: ok: imported. failed: pac failed, pac was not found, or a file changed before its import. unknown: the import timed out; it may have finished or still be running in the environment, so check the solution's import history. not-run: nothing was imported for it (the run stopped first or was refused). planned: a dry run would import it. skipped: its action is skip (not in a refusal, where every row is not-run).

pacExitCode.description: pac's exit code when it failed; null otherwise, also for a timeout or a changed file.

flows.description: The cloud flows of the planned installs and upgrades, in plan order; empty when the run was refused or failed, or nothing was imported.

solution.description: The unique name of the flow's solution.

expectedState.description: The state the plan predicted for the flow after the import.

stateAfter.description: The flow's state in the target after the imports, found by its id ('missing' when it is not there); null in a dry run or when the second read failed. Exit 1 when it differs from expectedState.

agents.description: The Copilot Studio agents of the zips the run would import (dry run) or did import (import 'ok'), in plan order; empty when there are none, or when nothing was imported. The read-back never changes status, message, solutions or the exit code. It has not yet run against a tenant, so 'missing' is a prompt to check in Copilot Studio, not proof.

solution.description: The unique name of the agent's solution.

state.description: null in a dry run. found: the read returned a bot row with this schema name. missing: it returned none, which also happens when the reading account can't see that agent. not-read: the read failed (a warning is on stderr), or the name is not one powerops sends (letters, digits and underscores, at most 100 characters).

publishedOn.description: For a found agent, whether the bot row's 'publishedon' is set; null otherwise. It does not say someone published the agent in the target, and for an upgrade or an agent the target already held it does not show what the import did.
